display_name: ISA Golden Thread Object Level Target, 0.5X

fiducials.notes:
Click the four outer corners of the patch strip itself: the top-left and bottom-left of patch 1, and the top-right and bottom-right of patch 30. The patches are butted squares against a grey card, so those corners are sharp. THE QUAD IS 34 PITCHES LONG AND ONE PATCH TALL: place it along the strip's own axis rather than the pixel grid. A strip laid down half a degree off square drifts a quarter of a patch height from end to end, and features off the patch row -- the printed rules especially -- then run out of their declared bands; clicking the real corners handles it, because the homography absorbs the rotation.

A third disc glued to the middle of the top edge, which some V2 cards carry in place of V1's printed centre disc, is ignored. The quad is fitted from the patch lattice in both axes, so the discs play no part in placement. On a capture of a V2 carrying a printed third dot, the strip places from 18 of its 34 slots at a lattice residual of 0.47 px, and the disc finder refuses every region of the frame, so the dot is not taken for a Device Level Target.

A frame holding both a Device Level Target and a dotted Object Level strip has not been measured. find_printed_discs runs once per region and can only combine discs it finds within one region.

printed_marks.count: three on the older version, two on the current one
printed_marks.notes: The strip prints solid dark discs, and HOW MANY DEPENDS ON THE VERSION. The older product -- no yellow border -- prints three: one at each end and one at the centre. The current product, revamped by ISA with a yellow border, a serial box and an 'All values are batch averages' caption, DROPPED THE CENTRE ONE and prints two. Measured positions in this definition's own frame: ends at u -0.0215 and +1.0214, agreeing between the two versions to 0.0003 of the strip -- one pixel in three thousand four hundred -- and the older version's centre disc at u +0.50003, dead centre, at v -0.429. Placement does not key on them because two points cannot define a quad and the third is not on every card; they are recorded because they are the best registered features on the target and are what an automatic placement should use, taking the centre disc as a bonus where it exists.

patch_grid.coordinate_frame: Relative to the patch strip's own bounding quad: patch 1's outer left corners to patch 30's outer right corners, taken along the strip's axis.
patch_grid.notes: PATCHES 1 TO 14, all at one pitch. Patch 15 is declared apart because it is not: see patches_left_end. TWO BLOCKS, NOT ONE LATTICE WITH HOLES. The 1X declares a single row of thirty-four slots of which four are the resolution module, because on that chart the module happens to span four patch pitches. On this one it spans 4.37, so no integer slot count describes the strip: a uniform lattice anchored on both ends puts patch 15's ROI 72 px off centre on a 267 px patch, which is the whole of the sampling inset's margin, and patch 1's ROI onto the printed disc beside the block. Each block therefore carries its own origin and its own pitch, which is what the schema's per-region grids are for and what the ISA transmissive charts' two wedges already do. The left block, patches 1 to 15, pitch 266.907 px on the capture this was measured from.

patch_grid.coordinate_frame: Relative to the patch strip's own bounding quad: patch 1's outer left corners to patch 30's outer right corners, taken along the strip's axis.
patch_grid.notes:
PATCH 15 IS CUT SHORT, which is why it is declared apart. Its neighbours are 266.9 px on the capture this was measured from and it is 178 -- it runs from the boundary with patch 14 to the printed keyline that ends the block, and the block's width is not a whole number of pitches. Sampled as a fifteenth equal cell, its ROI would overrun onto the keyline and the shadow beside it.

MEASURED ON ONE PHYSICAL UNIT, so whether the patch is clipped by design or this card was trimmed is not established. Sampling a narrower area than the patch costs a little averaging, where sampling wider puts something that is not the patch into the number.

regions.notes: The last patch of the left block, clipped where the block ends.

patch_grid.coordinate_frame: Relative to the patch strip's own bounding quad: patch 1's outer left corners to patch 30's outer right corners, taken along the strip's axis.
patch_grid.notes: TWO BLOCKS, NOT ONE LATTICE WITH HOLES. The 1X declares a single row of thirty-four slots of which four are the resolution module, because on that chart the module happens to span four patch pitches. On this one it spans 4.37, so no integer slot count describes the strip: a uniform lattice anchored on both ends puts patch 15's ROI 72 px off centre on a 267 px patch, which is the whole of the sampling inset's margin, and patch 1's ROI onto the printed disc beside the block. Each block therefore carries its own origin and its own pitch, which is what the schema's per-region grids are for and what the ISA transmissive charts' two wedges already do. The right block, patches 16 to 30, pitch 263.333 px. The two blocks' pitches differ by 1.4%, which is measured rather than assumed and is why they are not one grid at one pitch.

geometry.printed_label: centimetres, read on the millimetre comb
geometry.measured_note: 49 divisions at 82.02 px, scattering 0.95 px about a uniform pitch. THE 1X DECLARES ITS CENTIMETRE MAJORS INSTEAD, because its band had to read on two physical units whose combs sat four to six pixels apart and no declared band caught the 1 mm comb on both. There is one unit here and its comb reads, and finer divisions over the same span are the better-conditioned fit.

regions.notes: The millimetre rule, along the right half of the strip above the patches.

straight_edges.note: The lower boundary of the module's dark block, measured at 5.15 degrees with 93 samples scattering 0.33 px about the fitted line. NOT the block's upper boundary, which is 0.18 degrees off the strip's own axis -- axis-aligned edges repeat one sub-pixel phase on every row and carry nothing to oversample, and they are the highest-contrast boundaries in the module, so choosing edges by contrast chooses exactly the wrong ones.
The right-hand boundary of the module's left block, measured at -5.19 degrees with 115 samples scattering 0.31 px. Both edges are 472 px long on the capture this was measured from.

geometry.measured_note: Endpoints read off NMNH-USNMENT00316740.tif at full resolution and mapped into the quad through the placement, so they are stated in the chart's own frame rather than in one capture's pixels. The u values agree with the 1X's declaration to 0.003 and 0.001; the v values do not and cannot, because v is a fraction of the patch height and this chart's patches stand 1.49 times taller than wide where the 1X's are square. No roi_half_width override: the 1X needs one because its block is 60 px deep with the printed value table 25 px below it, and here the block is 108 px deep above the edge with plain card below.

regions.notes: The resolution module, between the two patch blocks.

nominal_values.source: The L*a*b* table printed on the card, read off two captures of two physical units. No per-unit measurements of this model are published.

reference_data.notes: A per-unit file is preferred and used whenever one is supplied. Failing that, the L*a*b* table printed on the card is the per-unit data and can be transcribed.
reference_data.sample_id_aliases_notes: Measurement files published for this target through the OpenQualia label standard name its patches 'A1'-'A30' where the chart itself prints '1'-'30'. The chart's own labels are used here, which is also what the OpenQualia measurement file standard specifies for a target labelled with numbers alone -- it names the Golden Thread Device and Object Level targets as its example of exactly that case. The correspondence is declared rather than guessed, is applied only when it matches more patches than reading the file as written, and is reported in the run's warnings when it is used. Verified against published per-unit measurements: all 30 patches matched, and their values agree with this definition's own batch-average nominals to a mean of 0.97 dE2000 (DLT unit D00011) and 0.81 dE2000 (Object Level unit M000559), which is the right magnitude for one unit against a batch mean.

tonal_response.notes: Twelve steps, D 0.05 to 2.38, at patches 10 to 21 -- the six either side of the resolution module. Ordered by the density OpenDICE states, which here is also their printed order.

white_balance.notes: Delta E(a*b*) against the reference chroma, L* excluded.

notes:
THE 0.5X IS NOT THE 1X SCALED. Its patches stand 1.49 times taller than wide where the 1X's are square, its two patch blocks sit at pitches 1.4% apart, and the module between them spans 4.37 pitches rather than a whole number -- so it is declared as two grids at their own origins, and no single lattice describes it. It prints the same batch table of L*a*b* values as the older 1X unit OpenDICE publishes as ObjectDICE.tif, which is what lets the two captures check each other digit for digit.

ONLY ONE RULE IS DECLARED, and the chart prints two. The inch comb reads at 1/8 inch and is regular -- its sixteen ticks span 259 to 262.5 px, a standard deviation of 1.2 -- but no declared band gets the fit below 3.0 px against a 1.5 px limit, because the braided keyline printed a few pixels beneath the ticks falls inside every band wide enough to catch them, and the projection's own low percentile then finds the keyline rather than the ticks. A rule that warns on every run is worse than a rule not declared.

THE CROSS-CHECK THE SECOND RULE WOULD HAVE BOUGHT WAS MADE ANYWAY, here, once: the inch comb measures 260.25 px per eighth and the millimetre comb 82.00 px per millimetre, which are 3.1730 mm and 3.1750 mm per eighth -- 0.06% apart. That is what says division_mm is right, and it is recorded because a single declared rule has nothing at run time to check it against.

measured_from.scale: 82.02 px/mm, from the chart's own two printed rules -- the eighth-inch comb at 260.5 px and the millimetre comb at 82.0 px, which agree to 0.06%
measured_from.module_gap: 4.37 pitches -- NOT an integer, which is why this chart cannot be declared as the 1X's single 34-slot lattice with four slots empty. A uniform 34-slot model anchored on both ends puts patch 15's ROI 72 px off centre on a 267 px patch, which is the whole of the sampling inset's margin.
measured_from.notes: Block boundaries read at full resolution against a drawn pixel scale. The strip's first comb tooth is the printed disc's edge, not patch 1's.
measured_from.verified: All twenty Smithsonian Odonata captures place automatically and read 2.37 to 2.57 dE2000 against the printed table -- a spread of 0.20 across twenty independent captures of one physical chart. On the capture the geometry was measured from, sixteen of the profile's seventeen metrics are judged; maximum modulation reads exactly 1.000 on both slanted edges and colour channel misregistration 0.116 px.
